description: Prose that carries BRACES at a `<program>` body-top — `try {this} at home`, `class {A} notes`, `class Room extends the house {with} doors`, `switch (on) {the lights} now`, a head split from its `{` across lines, a block holding markup — is page text and fires no §7.2.1 code (S441 review round false-positive guard).
rationale: SPEC §7.2.1: "Whether a construct is present SHALL be decided from the parsed program, never from source text" and "The word is not at fault." §40.8 S378 note: prose at the default-logic body-top renders and is a working shape. The S441 lift recognises only a construct written as a complete block — head and `{` on one line, a matching `}` in the run, a statement-shaped body with no markup, nothing but whitespace after the `}` (`try` needs `catch`/`finally`; `switch` needs a `case`/`default`) — so none of these shapes is a construct.
